purpose: Fidaxomicin is an antibiotic used to treat a bacterial infection in your gut called Clostridioides difficile, also known as C. diff. C. diff can cause severe diarrhea and stomach cramping. This medicine works right in your intestines to kill the bacteria causing your infection.
how_it_works: Fidaxomicin works by stopping the harmful C. diff bacteria from making the proteins they need to survive and multiply. Think of it like pulling the plug on the bacteria's power source. Because it mostly stays in your gut and doesn't get absorbed much into your bloodstream, it targets the infection right where it is causing problems.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, and constipation. Some people may also notice a drop in their blood counts, which your doctor may monitor with blood tests. Most side effects are mild, but let your doctor know if anything feels bothersome.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you are allergic to fidaxomicin or any other macrolide antibiotics like erythromycin or azithromycin. This medicine is meant only for C. diff infections and should not be used for other types of infections. If your diarrhea gets worse or you develop a fever, contact your doctor right away. Also let your doctor know about all other medications you take, as some can interact with this drug.
typical_dosing: The usual dose for adults is one 200 mg tablet taken by mouth twice a day, once in the morning and once in the evening, for 10 days. You can take it with or without food. Try to take it at the same times each day and finish the full course, even if you start feeling better sooner.
